transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Recording: Fireflies.ai auto
Attendees: Leah Carter (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anika Shah (Redwood), Daniel Park (EdgeGrid CTO), Sofia Martins (EdgeGrid Head Eng), Ravi Gupta (Infra), Elena Rovira (Partnerships)

Summary: Intro-level partner discovery between Redwood and EdgeGrid Systems focused on on-prem GPU deployments and potential reseller/integration partnership. High-level compatibility questions on drivers, networking, and security. Agreement to run a micro-benchmark and schedule deeper SE-led technical dive.

Topics covered: on-prem installer vs containerized agent; GPU driver/version compatibility; model weight distribution and storage; network latency and NVLink/NVSwitch topologies; KMS/HSM integration for keys; legal/commercial sequencing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Leah (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intros? We'll keep this to about 45 minutes and then sync on next steps.
[00:12] Daniel (EdgeGrid): Yep hi, Daniel here — CTO at EdgeGrid, we do turnkey GPU clusters for telco and enterprise customers, happy to talk through ops and partner models.
[00:20] Sofia (EdgeGrid): Sofia — head of eng, I mainly care about deployment templates and day 2 ops.
[00:26] Leah: Great — Marco, do you want to say hi and outline what we can cover?
[00:30] Marco (Redwood SE): Sure — Marco Ruiz, SE. I'll focus on runtime compatibility, kernels, perf expectations; want to understand your hardware and how you prefer packaging (installer vs docker image).
[00:42] Ravi (EdgeGrid): Hi, Ravi, infra lead. We run mixed Nvidia A100 and H100 racks, some with MIG configs, NVLink expected in some clusters.
[00:52] Marco: Perfect — that helps. Quick question: are you more interested in a reseller partnership where you package Redwood Private as part of EdgeGrid offering, or a tight technical integration/certification where we jointly ship an image?
[01:10] Elena (Partnerships): From partnerships side we want both options on the table — some customers want turnkey preinstalled nodes, others want a certified container they can pull.
[01:20] Leah: Right — Redwood supports private deployments in two primary forms: a managed control plane option for partner-hosted VPCs and an on-prem package for air-gapped customers. Marco can give the nitty-gritty.
[01:30] Marco: Technical overview: Redwood runtime picks kernels based on model architecture and seq-length distribution; we rely on CUDA/cuDNN and optimized fused kernels for many ops. For H100s we use the updated kernels and different memory planner. That means we need driver versions >=X.Y and specific lib versions — we'll share the exact matrix.
[01:50] Daniel: When you say "matrix" — is that per model or per hardware? We run multiple generations in parallel; we don't want to maintain ten separate stacks.
[02:00] Marco: Good question. The runtime is compatible with a range but we offer a recommended stack per family (A100, H100). We do have fallbacks to less optimized kernels when versions differ, but expect a perf delta.
[02:18] Sofia: What's the upgrade story? If we push a kernel or driver upgrade, is there rolling restart support?
[02:25] Marco: Yes — we have node draining and rolling binary updates; for on-prem we provide a package/installer that orchestrates it. Some customers prefer containerized deployment to decouple host drivers from runtime. There's a trade-off.
[02:40] Ravi: Storage: large model weights — do you expect local SSD on each node or central NFS? We also have Ceph clusters.
[02:48] Marco: We support multiple patterns. Recommended is local NVMe cache for hot weights plus central object store (S3/GCS compatible) for cold-storage. We also support streaming weights and quantized formats to reduce IO.
[03:06] Daniel: Security — we're heavily regulated. KMS integration, HSM for keys, SOC2 type questions.
[03:12] Anika (Redwood): We support KMS integrations and can plug into customer-managed KMS/HSM; audit logs and RBAC are part of the Private feature set. We'll share SOC2 docs and typical compliance checklist.
[03:26] Sofia: Also curious about telemetry — can we control what telemetry is sent back to Redwood? Some customers need zero egress.
[03:34] Leah: Yes — for air-gapped deployments telemetry can be disabled; for managed private control planes we have opt-in telemetry with retention controls and request-level sanitization.
[03:45] Marco: Perf question — what's your typical inference workload? Tokens per request, beam sizes, batching expectations? That'll determine batching and batching targets.
[03:55] Ravi: Most are chatty: conversation-style, avg 150 tokens per request, peak bursts with many short requests. We expect latency SLOs sub-150ms at tail for smaller models, more lenient for larger fine-tuned models.
[04:12] Marco: That sounds workload-y. We'll propose batching/caching profile suggestions and where to use prefix KV caching to hit tail latency targets.
[04:28] Daniel: Any requirement on network topology? We do NVLink within node, NVSwitch across a pod, but between racks it's 100GbE. Does Redwood require RDMA?
[04:39] Marco: Not required but beneficial for very large models and sharded KV caches. We can operate over 100GbE but performance implications for model sharding; we'll note those in the benchmark plan.
[04:55] Sofia: Have you done certification with DGX or similar?
[05:00] Marco: Yes — we've run on DGX and also consumer-like racks. Differences are mostly around interconnect and driver stacks. We'll surface a compatibility table.
[05:12] (crosstalk)
[05:14] Elena: Commercial model — are you open to reseller margin or certified partner fee?
[05:18] Leah: We have flexible models: reseller arrangements and partner-certified deployments. Typically commercial terms are discussed after technical validation and a pilot.
[05:28] Daniel: Pilot — how long? What's in scope?
[05:31] Marco: Pilot usually 2–6 weeks: deploy runtime in a single cluster, run micro-benchmarks (throughput + tail latency), validate KMS and logging, and run a small sample of production traffic. We'll define success criteria up front.
[05:45] Ravi: For micro-benchmarks, will you supply the workload generator?
[05:49] Marco: Yes — we'll share a benchmark harness and recommended prompt sets. We'll also ask for a small representative dataset.
[05:58] Sofia: Any concerns around model licensing or weights? If we want to bundle open models is there anything we need to do?
[06:05] Leah: Usually customers bring the weights or we reference open model repos; licensing depends on the model. Redwood curates a catalog of verified open models — we can discuss model licensing per deployment.
[06:20] Daniel: For sales ops: do you want EdgeGrid to preinstall for customers or to sell the software-only option?
[06:27] Elena: We want both — preinstalled turnkey for telco customers and a certified software image for others.
[06:33] Leah: OK that works. We'll propose two tracks: 1) Certified image + certification guide, 2) Turnkey preinstall with ops runbook and optional training.
[06:48] Marco: One more technical note: quantization and kernel selection. If you plan to offer int8 quantized models, we'll need to validate kernels as some fused ops change. We'll include test vectors.
[07:00] Ravi: For H100, some customers expect MIG-like partitioning; do you support multi-tenant on the same GPU?
[07:08] Marco: We support MIG in the sense of isolating workloads but performance depends on model size. We'll include guidance.
[07:16] (silence)
[07:20] Leah: Ok quick pause — this is great. Want to open for any blockers or regulatory red flags?
[07:28] Daniel: Data residency and audit readiness. Need to ensure logs and prompts do not leave the customer boundary.
[07:34] Anika: Understood — Private can be configured with zero egress, plus audit logs are local and can be integrated with customer SIEM. We'll send the SOC2 and security whitepaper.
[07:48] Sofia: Can we do a non-functional perf target: 95th percentile latency <200ms for 8-token responses on small models under 50RPS?
[07:58] Marco: Sounds feasible with right batching, KV cache and local NVMe. We'll measure in the micro-benchmark.
[08:06] Daniel: Operational runbook — who handles updates? EdgeGrid or customer?
[08:11] Leah: Both options — we can do co-managed or handoff. For reseller turnkey, EdgeGrid ops would maintain the image, for software-only, customer handles host updates.
[08:22] (background noise — someone typing)
[08:26] Elena: Timeline — if we want to go to market H2 2025, when should we kick pilot?
[08:33] Leah: Ideally pilot start in early June to give time for cert and docs; that aligns with your H2 goal.
[08:39] Marco: We'll need spec sheet from Ravi to finalize pilot infra.
[08:44] Ravi: I'll drop that in the shared folder after the call.
[08:48] Leah: Great — on legal, we'll send NDA and SOW template. Elena, do you want to loop in commercial terms after we validate tech?
[08:57] Elena: Yes please.
[09:00] Marco: Quick note — we sometimes see mis-transcriptions in automated notes: NVLink vs N V Link — lol — just making sure ops knows exact terms.
[09:07] (light laughter)
[09:10] Leah: Alright let's close with a recap and next steps.
[09:14] Leah: Recap: Redwood to provide architecture doc, benchmark harness, and driver compatibility matrix. EdgeGrid to share cluster specs. Legal teams to exchange NDA/SOW. Schedule SE deep dive week of 6/2.
[09:29] Daniel: Sounds good.
[09:30] Leah: Thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.
